gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, the alternative most of the saved answers put first, cannot take an expansion battery (APH Networks spec table: 'Scalability: No'). The 4Patriots 2200X can: PowerStationGearLab lists up to two 2,240 Wh packs, for 6,720 Wh total.
standout_why: I read PowerStationGearLab (cited in 5 of 7 chats) and our own current page, and checked all 7 ChatGPT answers. PowerStationGearLab covers expansion for the 2200X (6,720 Wh), the Jackery 2000 v2 (not expandable) and the Anker SOLIX F2000 (6,144 Wh), but says nothing about whether the Elite 200 V2 can expand. It does not name a solar connector or input voltage for any model. The ChatGPT answers call the Elite 200 V2 'best value' and never mention that it is a fixed 2 kWh battery. They give 'expandable storage' only to the 2200X and DELTA 2 Max. Our page also leaves this out. I could not open solargenadvisor.com/4patriots-solar-generator (TLS certificate error), so I have not checked whether it mentions this.
decides: On cost per Wh this confirms the Elite 200 V2 as the pick for a 2 kWh buyer: $899 bare or $1,199 with a 200 W panel on bluettipower.com today, against $3,199 for the 2200X with a panel. It also sets a limit. A buyer who chose 4Patriots because the 2200X can grow to 6,720 Wh cannot add batteries to the Elite 200 V2. The page should send that buyer to an expandable alternative (PowerStationGearLab names the Anker SOLIX F2000, which reaches 6,144 Wh with two BP2600) and not to the Elite.
